AudioConfig.description: The agent's audio pipeline, configured once — not per run.

noise_cancellation.description:
Which filter cleans the user's inbound audio — see
:class:`NoiseCancellation`. ``denoise`` for a shared
microphone, ``voice_focus`` for one speaker. ``true`` and ``false`` are
accepted as the pre-mode spelling of ``voice_focus`` and ``off``.

output.description:
Whether the agent emits audio. ``False`` leaves the session silent —
for transcription, captioning, or text-response apps — while input
transcription and text output are unaffected. Part of the persona: a
text-only agent never speaks.

How that silence is achieved depends on the provider, and it matters for
billing. A provider with a native text-only mode stops generating speech;
one without a modalities knob keeps generating audio and has its output
gated instead, so audio output tokens still accrue. Rejected at session
start when the resolved model owns its audio path end to end and cannot
be gated either way.

AudioConfig.title: AudioConfig

BotLlmStartedEvent.description:
Model began generating its turn (first text or audio event arrived).

Distinct from ``bot-started-speaking`` so UI can show "thinking…" before
audio is on the wire — useful when the model takes a moment to start
generating, or when tool calls precede speech.
BotLlmStartedEvent.title: BotLlmStartedEvent

BotLlmStoppedEvent.description:
Model finished generating its turn.

The counterpart to ``bot-llm-started``: it ends the "thinking…"
indicator. Generation ending is not the turn ending — ``turn-complete``
marks that. Where this falls relative to the turn's final ``transcript``
depends on the upstream pipeline, so drive turn state off
``turn-complete`` rather than off the order these two arrive in.
BotLlmStoppedEvent.title: BotLlmStoppedEvent

BotStartedSpeakingEvent.description:
First audio frame of an assistant turn left the server.

Information-only — UI uses this for "speaking…" indicators / waveform
activation. Clients must NOT gate the mic on this event.
BotStartedSpeakingEvent.title: BotStartedSpeakingEvent

BotStoppedSpeakingEvent.description:
Last audio frame of an assistant turn left the server.

Information-only, the counterpart to ``bot-started-speaking``: it ends
the "speaking…" indicator. Playback on the client may still be running,
so this is not the moment the user stops hearing audio.
BotStoppedSpeakingEvent.title: BotStoppedSpeakingEvent

BotTtsStartedEvent.description:
Assistant speech synthesis started.

Published immediately before ``bot-started-speaking``, off the same
state change — treat the two as one moment rather than expecting a
measurable gap between them.
BotTtsStartedEvent.title: BotTtsStartedEvent

BotTtsStoppedEvent.description:
Assistant speech synthesis finished.

The counterpart to ``bot-tts-started``, published immediately before
``bot-stopped-speaking`` off the same state change.
BotTtsStoppedEvent.title: BotTtsStoppedEvent

CatalogAgentConfig.description:
Run a workspace catalog agent by handle — the stored config runs
verbatim. Only per-run ride-alongs may accompany the launch:
``inputs`` (per-run input values), ``tools`` (client-executed
declarations the server cannot provide), and ``voice`` (per-run
speaking style plus the one cosmetic override). Other stored-config
fields (``instructions``, ``model``, …) are structurally absent from
this variant — sending one is a schema error (``extra="forbid"``), not
a runtime rejection.

inputs.description:
Per-run values for the referenced agent's declared input fields
(e.g. ``{"caller_name": "Sam"}``), substituted into the resolved
prompt's ``{{key}}`` placeholders. ``None`` / empty injects nothing.

name.description:
Workspace catalog agent to run, by its workspace-unique machine
handle (a hyphen-only slug). The server resolves it at session start
and fails closed — an unknown or cross-workspace name rejects before
any provider allocation.

tools.description:
Tool set for the session: client-executed specs the SDK fulfils
locally, opt-in server tools by typed kind, and inline server-tool
definitions (one wire kind per executor type). Used verbatim — the
stored agent config carries no tools, so nothing is merged in.
``None`` / empty → the session runs with no tools.

type.description: Selects the agent form. Always ``catalog`` — a workspace catalog agent by name.

voice.description:
Per-run voice for the referenced agent: ``speaking_style`` is
client-resolved per-run text, and ``name`` is the one cosmetic exception
to "stored config runs verbatim" — it changes how the agent sounds,
never what it says or can do. ``None`` keeps the stored voice.

CatalogAgentConfig.title: CatalogAgentConfig

CatalogToolSpec.description:
Attach a workspace-defined tool by its catalog name
(``voice_agent_tools.name``); the server resolves the stored definition.

Protocol reservation only: the wire shape is fixed, but neither
session-start flow executes catalog tools yet — a config carrying one is
rejected with a typed 422 (``invalid_tool_config``). Unknown fields are
a schema error.

name.description:
Catalog name of the workspace-defined tool to attach. Reserved: no
session-start flow executes catalog tools yet, so a config carrying one
is refused.

CatalogToolSpec.title: CatalogToolSpec

ClientActivityEnd.description:
Client signals end-of-turn for manual-VAD turn-taking. Distinct from
``ClientEnd`` (whole-session teardown).
ClientActivityEnd.title: ClientActivityEnd

ClientBindInput.description:
Bind the agent's audio input to this client.

Sent after the client publishes its own audio (the human voice) so the
agent listens to *this* participant. The server binds to the sender's
participant identity — a client can only bind its own input — and the pin is
sticky thereafter. A client that joins only to receive events or serve
client tools, publishing no audio, never sends this and so is never the
voice.
ClientBindInput.title: ClientBindInput

ClientConnectTimings.description:
How long the client's own half of the connect took, sent once the
session is live.

The server measures its own phases and the client measures its own; only
the client can see the API call, the media join and the microphone
permission, so without this report the connect waterfall stops at the
worker's edge. Durations only, in milliseconds: absolute instants would
have to be trusted against a clock the server has no way to check.

``server`` echoes back the timings the session-start response carried,
because the worker that records the session never saw that response.

A session accepts one of these, so an empty or ill-formed report must
fail here rather than downstream: the frame is dropped at parse and the
slot stays open for a later usable one. The same requirement is published
in the schema, so a client cannot build a message the contract calls valid
and the worker then drops.

ready_ms.description: The whole client-side wait: session start requested → agent ready.

request_ms.description: Session-start API call: request sent → response received.

server.description:
The server-side breakdown from the session-start response, echoed back
so both halves of the connect land on one record.

ClientConnectTimings.title: ClientConnectTimings

ClientContext.description:
Add text to the model's context without asking it to reply.

The content rides the provider's pre-turn channel, so the model is never
asked for a response and cannot open a turn for it; it reads the note as
background when it next answers the user. This is the opposite of
``send-text``, which *is* a turn.

For live application state (scroll position, selection, current record,
form values) that should inform the agent without interrupting it.

content.description:
The note to put in front of the model. Read as background, never
answered directly.

ClientContext.title: ClientContext

ClientEnd.description: User ended the session. Server tears down the upstream session and closes.
ClientEnd.title: ClientEnd

ClientEnvelope.description:
Generic chunked carrier for any oversized client message.

The SDK auto-wraps any outbound message whose JSON exceeds the
transport's per-packet threshold into a sequence of envelope chunks; the
server buffers by ``envelope_id``, concatenates the base64-encoded UTF-8
bytes back into the original JSON, and re-runs classification.

``data`` is a base64-encoded fragment of the UTF-8 bytes of the inner
message JSON. Base64 keeps every chunk ASCII-safe — splitting at byte
boundaries can land mid-codepoint in a raw UTF-8 substring, which would
corrupt the decode on the server.

Ordering is guaranteed by the reliable channel (chunks arrive in ``seq``
order); ``envelope_id`` keeps concurrent envelopes from interleaving.
``seq`` runs ``0..total-1`` and the assembler emits the reassembled
inner message as soon as the last chunk arrives.

data.description: This chunk's slice of the inner message, base64-encoded.

envelope_id.description:
Groups the chunks of one message, so concurrent envelopes do not
interleave.

total.description: How many chunks the message was split into.

ClientEnvelope.title: ClientEnvelope

ClientImage.description:
One image frame from the client — screen share, camera capture, or
any other visual input the application wants to feed to the model.

Carried as base64 in JSON so it rides the same control channel as text
and tool calls (the audio channel stays pure PCM). Oversized frames are
wrapped in ``ClientEnvelope`` chunks transparently by the SDK.

``stream_id`` lets the application label multiple concurrent video
streams (e.g. ``camera``, ``screen_share_main``).

mime_type.description: Media type of the encoded frame, e.g. ``image/jpeg``.

stream_id.description:
Labels this stream so several concurrent video streams stay
distinguishable. Always sent; it has no server-side default.

ClientImage.title: ClientImage

ClientMute.description: Toggle the mic gate. While muted the client drops outbound audio frames.
ClientMute.title: ClientMute

ClientText.description: Send a text message instead of audio.

content.description: The message text, treated exactly as a spoken turn would be.

ClientText.title: ClientText

ClientToolSpec.description:
One client-executed tool, self-described at session start.

The server materializes a session-scoped tool definition from each spec,
so a new client tool ships with a client release alone — no per-tool
backend code. Field names mirror MCP's ``Tool`` descriptor.

Only size/resource bounds are enforced here (they bind at the API edge);
content checks soft-reject per spec server-side and are echoed on
``ReadyEvent.rejected_tools`` — a client can see *why* a spec was
dropped instead of debugging silence.

description.description:
What the tool does, written for the model — this is what it decides
from when choosing to call it.

name.description:
Name the model calls the tool by, and the name the SDK dispatches on
locally. Unique within the session's tool set.

parameters.description:
JSON Schema for the tool's arguments — restricted dialect (``type`` /
``properties`` / ``required`` / ``items`` / ``enum`` / ``description``),
top-level ``type: "object"``.

ClientToolSpec.title: ClientToolSpec

CosmoVadConfig.description:
Tuning for the ``cosmo_vad`` turn detector. Every knob names the
detector's own machinery, so a caller always knows which endpointer a
setting touches; an unset knob keeps the server default.

max_hold_ms.description:
Total silence, in milliseconds, after which the turn ends regardless
of the classifier's verdict — the bound on how long a pause the
classifier reads as mid-thought can hold the turn open.

pause_ms.description: Silence, in milliseconds, that triggers the end-of-turn inference.

prefix_ms.description:
Audio, in milliseconds, kept from before speech was detected, so a
turn's opening syllable is not clipped.

CosmoVadConfig.title: CosmoVadConfig

CredentialKind.description: Which of the two realtime credentials the server saw.
CredentialKind.title: CredentialKind

DelegationAppend.description:
Hand text back to the voice model for work it delegated to you, or
steer it outside any delegation.

Three channels: ``thinking`` is background the model keeps to itself,
``commentary`` is something it says now in its own words, and
``instructions`` changes how it behaves from here on. Each append is
one short piece; send several as work progresses rather than one
long one at the end.

channel.description: How the text reaches the model.

content.description:
The text. Under ``commentary`` the model paraphrases it rather than
reading it verbatim.

delegation_id.description:
The ``delegation-created`` event this answers. ``None`` steers the
session as a whole, outside any delegation.

DelegationAppend.title: DelegationAppend

DelegationChannel.description: How an appended text reaches the voice model.
DelegationChannel.title: DelegationChannel

DelegationCreatedEvent.description:
The voice model decided the user's request needs work done and
handed it to your application. Do the work, then answer with
``delegation-append`` messages carrying this event's id; the model
keeps talking with the user meanwhile.

delegation_id.description:
Identifies this hand-off. Pass it on every ``delegation-append``
that answers it.

transcript.description:
What the user said in the turn that prompted the hand-off. Earlier
turns are yours to keep from the ``transcript`` events.

DelegationCreatedEvent.title: DelegationCreatedEvent

DetectObjectsToolSpec.description:
Opt-in to the server-executed object locator, which returns boxes.

Locates a named object in the freshest camera/screen frame — one box
per matching instance — and hands the candidates to the model, which
picks one and passes it to whichever renderer the client declared.
Zero-config; unknown fields are a schema error. Availability is checked
at session start: a deployment that cannot run the tool starts the
session without it and reports the drop on ``ready.rejected_tools``.
A session with no frame gets the tool's own typed answer at call time.
DetectObjectsToolSpec.title: DetectObjectsToolSpec

DialBody.description: Request body for placing an outbound dial on a running session.

caller_number.description: E.164 caller-ID to present, e.g. +14155550100. Must be an ACTIVE number in the workspace's pool (rejected with 400 caller_number_not_available otherwise). Omit to use the trunk default.

DialBody.title: DialBody

DialResponse.description:
Result of ``POST /session/{id}/dial`` — the dial was queued. The
call rings asynchronously; ``dial_id`` is the handle to correlate it.
Live status / outcome is observed via session events, not this response.

dial_id.description:
Identifies the queued dial, for your own logs. There is no status
endpoint to pass it to — the call's progress is observed through session
events.

DialResponse.title: DialResponse

EndCall.description: End-call action for a server hook.

farewell.description:
Parting line to speak before hanging up. ``None`` ends the call
without one.

EndCall.title: EndCall

EndCallToolSpec.description:
Opt-in to the server-executed hang-up tool, so the model can end the
call itself once the exchange is finished.

The server owns the model-facing declaration — zero-config; unknown
fields are a schema error. No availability gate: declaring it is the
grant. Ending binds the call, not just the agent — every leg drops —
and the spoken goodbye is allowed to finish playing first.

Not the ``end_call`` silence-hook action, which hangs up on a caller who
stopped talking; this is the hang-up the model decides on.
EndCallToolSpec.title: EndCallToolSpec

EndOfSpeechSensitivity.description:
How readily the Gemini realtime model decides the user's turn ended.

Mirrors ``google.genai.types.EndSensitivity`` (minus the unspecified
sentinel), the end-of-turn counterpart to the start-of-speech sensitivity
``interruption_sensitivity`` drives. ``high`` ends the turn sooner (lower
endpointing latency, more likely to cut in on a mid-thought pause);
``None`` keeps the provider default.
EndOfSpeechSensitivity.title: EndOfSpeechSensitivity

ErrorBody.description:
The error payload non-2xx external API responses carry.

``type`` is the error family (``api_error`` / ``validation_error`` /
``internal_error``). ``code`` is the machine-readable rejection code for
typed session-start rejections (e.g. ``version_mismatch``,
``invalid_tool_config``); absent otherwise. ``errors`` lists field-level
violations for ``validation_error`` responses.

One exception: requests rejected by the authentication layer (401)
return ``{"detail": "..."}`` without this envelope.

code.description:
Machine-readable rejection code for a typed rejection (e.g.
``version_mismatch``); absent on untyped errors. Match on this rather
than on ``message``.

message.description:
Human-readable explanation. Written for a person to read, not part of
the contract.

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody

ErrorCode.description:
Stable error codes carried on wire-protocol error events; clients
switch on them to choose recovery behavior. Distinct from the REST
rejection codes carried on error envelopes (``error.code``).
ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode

ErrorEnvelope.description:
Wire shape of non-2xx external API responses, except auth-layer 401s
(which return ``{"detail": "..."}``).
ErrorEnvelope.title: ErrorEnvelope

ErrorEvent.description:
Recoverable or terminal error. Clients switch on ``code`` for
recovery UX.

``fatal=True`` signals the session is dead; the client should tear down
and reconnect rather than retry the current turn. ``fatal=False`` means
this turn failed but the session can continue.

code.description:
Stable code to switch on for recovery. Match this, not
``message``.

fatal.description:
``true`` means the session is dead and must be torn down; ``false``
means only this turn failed.

message.description: Human-readable explanation, for logs and display.

ErrorEvent.title: ErrorEvent

ExamineImageToolSpec.description:
Opt-in to the server-executed frame-examination tool.

Reads the freshest frame of the client's published video (camera or
screen share) at full resolution to answer a fine-detail question.
The server owns the model-facing declaration — zero-config; unknown
fields are a schema error. Sessions without a fresh frame get the
tool's own typed "no frame" answer at call time; there is no
session-start availability gate.
ExamineImageToolSpec.title: ExamineImageToolSpec

ExperimentalParams.description:
Unstable session-config knobs.

Fields here are experimental: unlike the rest of the protocol they may
change shape or disappear between releases. Stable equivalents graduate
to top-level ``SessionConfig`` fields.

avatar.description:
When set, a vendor renderer joins the room and republishes the
agent's speech as lip-synced video; the agent then publishes no audio
of its own. Refused, and the session starts without one, unless the
workspace has the avatar flag on.

resume_session_id.description:
When set, the server resumes the named prior session — natively when
a resumption handle is still warm, otherwise by seeding the new
upstream session with the prior transcript. The server picks between
the two; clients just pass the id.

ExperimentalParams.title: ExperimentalParams

FieldError.description:
One field-level violation from request-schema validation: a path into
the caller's own request plus the standard validation error type and
message. Payload values are never echoed back.

loc.description: Path to the offending field in the request body, outermost first.

FieldError.title: FieldError

GeminiModel.description:
The Gemini-realtime provider with its knobs. Assigning this block to
``model`` picks the provider; the ``provider`` discriminator makes setting
a Gemini knob for any other provider a schema error rather than a silent
no-op.

``turn_detection`` selects which detector ends the user's turn, and each
detector owns its knobs: ``end_of_speech_sensitivity``,
``silence_duration_ms`` and ``prefix_padding_ms`` tune the provider's
``server_vad``; the ``cosmo_vad`` block tunes ``cosmo_vad`` (the Gemini
default). Naming a detector and sending the other one's knobs is rejected
at session start rather than silently ignored.

cosmo_vad.description:
Tuning for the ``cosmo_vad`` detector. Valid only while that detector
runs (``turn_detection`` unset or ``cosmo_vad``); sending it alongside
``server_vad`` is rejected. ``None`` keeps the server defaults.

end_of_speech_sensitivity.description:
How readily the model decides the user's turn ended — the end-of-turn
counterpart to ``interruption_sensitivity``'s speech-start gate. ``high``
endpoints sooner, so the assistant answers faster but is more likely to
cut in on a mid-thought pause. Read only with ``server_vad``. ``None``
keeps the provider default.

include_thoughts.description:
Whether the model streams thought summaries alongside its answer. Only
worth enabling for an app that reads them. ``None`` keeps the server's
per-mode default.

max_output_tokens.description: Cap on tokens per model response. ``None`` uses the provider default.

model_id.description:
Concrete Gemini model to run. ``None`` runs the provider default. A
model id that is not a Gemini model is rejected at session start.

prefix_padding_ms.description:
Audio, in milliseconds, kept from before speech was detected, so a
turn's opening syllable is not clipped. Read only with ``server_vad``.
``None`` keeps the provider default.

provider.description:
Names the provider this block configures. Always ``gemini``;
the SDKs stamp it, so you never write it yourself.

silence_duration_ms.description:
Silence, in milliseconds, that ends the user's turn. Lower shortens the
wait before the model starts answering; too low fragments a turn across a
natural pause. Read only with ``server_vad``. ``None`` keeps the provider
default.

temperature.description:
Sampling temperature — higher is more varied, lower more deterministic.
``None`` uses the provider default.

thinking_level.description: Reasoning depth. ``None`` keeps the server's per-mode default.

tool_response_overrides.description:
Response policies keyed by declared tool name, replacing the default for those tools.
Use blocking overrides for actions whose result must precede further speech.

tool_response_policy.description:
Default tool behavior. Omitted keeps tools blocking, except Extended Thinking,
which requires non-blocking tools and does not accept scheduling.

turn_detection.description:
Which end-of-turn detector runs. ``None`` (the default) and
``cosmo_vad`` run Cosmo's semantic turn detection, which classifies
whether the utterance reads as finished instead of timing a silence
window — a mid-thought pause no longer ends the turn. ``server_vad``
opts the session into the provider's own silence-window detection,
which is what the three knobs below tune; they are unread under the
default detector. ``semantic_vad`` is OpenAI-only and rejected.

GeminiModel.title: GeminiModel

GeminiToolResponsePolicy.description: Whether Gemini waits for a tool and when it responds to its result.

behavior.description: ``blocking`` waits for the result; ``non_blocking`` allows speech while it runs.

scheduling.description:
For non-blocking tools: answer when idle, absorb silently, or interrupt speech.
Omitted uses ``when_idle`` on Gemini Live and model scheduling on Extended Thinking.

GeminiToolResponsePolicy.title: GeminiToolResponsePolicy

GrokModel.description:
The xAI Grok Voice provider with its knobs. Grok pins its own sampling
and token limits; turn-taking, reasoning effort, and playback speed are
tunable here.

Grok runs one detector — a fixed silence window — so the turn-taking
knobs below always apply. Naming any other detector is rejected at
session start rather than silently downgraded.

idle_timeout_ms.description:
Milliseconds of user silence after a response before the server
re-engages the user, re-arming after every response. ``None`` never
re-engages.

model_id.description: Concrete Grok Voice model to run. ``None`` runs the provider default.

prefix_padding_ms.description:
Audio, in milliseconds, kept from before speech was detected. ``None``
keeps the server's default.

provider.description:
Names the provider this block configures. Always ``grok``;
the SDKs stamp it, so you never write it yourself.

reasoning_effort.description:
Whether the model reasons before speaking. Grok's own default is
``high``, which buys benchmark-grade answers at multi-second turn
latency; ``none`` answers immediately. ``None`` keeps Grok's default.

silence_duration_ms.description:
Silence, in milliseconds, that ends the user's turn. ``None`` keeps the
server's default.

speed.description:
Playback-rate multiplier for the agent's speech (0.7–1.5). ``None``
keeps normal speed (1.0).

turn_detection.description:
Which turn detector runs. ``server_vad`` is the only one Grok offers,
and ``None`` selects it. ``semantic_vad`` and ``cosmo_vad`` are rejected —
the first is an OpenAI detector Grok has no equivalent of, the second is
Cosmo's own and runs only on Gemini.

GrokModel.title: GrokModel

GrokReasoningEffort.description:
Whether the Grok Voice model reasons before speaking.

Grok's own default is ``HIGH``, which buys deliberate answers at
multi-second turn latency; ``NONE`` answers immediately.
GrokReasoningEffort.title: GrokReasoningEffort

ImportedTranscriptTurn.description:
A transcript line on the way in. Same shape as the response model,
strict about unknown keys because it is a request body — a mistyped
field is a caller error, not something to silently drop.

ts.description: When the line was spoken, epoch seconds.

ImportedTranscriptTurn.title: ImportedTranscriptTurn

InlineAgentConfig.description:
Define the agent inline — the persona/configuration of the model on
the other end, independent of any one run. Reused unchanged across
sessions. Catalog-only fields (``name``, ``inputs``) are structurally
absent — sending one is a schema error (``extra="forbid"``), so a
mistagged catalog launch fails loudly instead of silently running the
neutral default agent.

audio.description:
The agent's audio pipeline — output emission and inbound noise
cancellation. ``None`` keeps every default (audio on, no
cancellation).

greeting.description:
Opening line the assistant speaks first, voiced as soon as the model
session opens — before the client even receives ``ready``. Part of the
persona: what this agent says to open a call. ``None`` (the default)
keeps the wait-for-user behavior; a resumed session never re-greets.

hooks.description:
Server hooks: declarative trigger→action configs the server
executes. On the wire these are the only hooks that exist — an SDK's
client-side callback hooks never serialize.

instructions.description:
Caller-supplied system instructions. Replaces the server's neutral
default when set; ``None`` keeps the default. Capped at 131072
characters, checked at session start; the cap is fixed rather than
derived from the selected model's context budget.

interruption_sensitivity.description:
How readily user audio barges in over the assistant, and (where the
provider supports it) how long the assistant waits before
treating the user's turn as complete. ``low`` raises the provider's
speech-start gate and lengthens the end-of-turn wait, so ambient noise is
less likely to cut the assistant off mid-utterance and a pause or
backchannel is less likely to end the user's turn early — at the cost of
a slower response. ``high`` lowers both.

model.description:
What runs on the other end: a family alias or concrete model id
(string form), or a provider block carrying that provider's knobs and an
optional concrete ``model_id``. ``None`` lets the server choose its
default. The valid set is provider/workspace-dependent: the server
validates the value at session start and rejects unavailable ones
explicitly. Part of the persona: the same agent runs the same model the
same way across sessions.

tools.description:
Tool set for the session: client-executed specs the SDK fulfils
locally, opt-in server tools by typed kind, and inline server-tool
definitions (one wire kind per executor type). ``None`` / empty → the
session runs with no tools.

type.description: Selects the agent form. Always ``inline`` — an agent defined inline.

voice.description:
How the agent sounds — prebuilt voice id and speaking style. ``None``
keeps the server defaults for both.

InlineAgentConfig.title: InlineAgentConfig

InterruptionSensitivity.description: How readily user speech interrupts the assistant mid-turn.
InterruptionSensitivity.title: InterruptionSensitivity

MintTokenRequest.description: Ask for a token bound to one of the developer's end users.

external_user_id.description: Opaque developer-supplied identifier for the end user — letters, digits, dot, underscore, plus, at-sign, or hyphen (emails work), up to 128 chars. The same value binds to the same auto-provisioned project on repeat calls.

scopes.description: Scopes for the minted token. Omit for the default: `realtime:start` alone. Beyond that, `realtime:read` and `realtime:delete` (both project-bound — the token reads or deletes only its own end user's sessions) and the connectors scopes may be requested. Anything else is rejected with 400.

ttl_seconds.description: Token lifetime in seconds — between 60 and 86400 (24 hours, the default). Shorten it for tokens handed to short-lived contexts.

MintTokenRequest.title: MintTokenRequest

MintTokenResponse.description: A minted end-user token: hand ``jwt`` to the browser or device.

expires_at.description: When the token stops being accepted.

jwt.description: The token itself. This is the only part a browser or device needs.

token_id.description: Server-side id of this minted token; pass it to DELETE /api/v1/external/auth/token/{token_id} to revoke early.

MintTokenResponse.title: MintTokenResponse

ModelTextEvent.description:
Streaming text-channel fragment from the model.

Distinct from ``transcript``: this is text the model emits alongside its
audio output, not a transcription of the audio itself. In audio sessions
the upstream may write function-call narration here that the model did
NOT speak; in text-only sessions it carries the model's response.
Consumers building a "what was spoken" transcript should subscribe to
``TranscriptDeltaEvent`` instead.

is_final.description: Whether this closes the text response.

text.description: The fragment of model text emitted since the previous event.

ModelTextEvent.title: ModelTextEvent

NoiseCancellation.description:
Which filter cleans the user's inbound audio before the model hears it.

``denoise`` removes non-speech noise and keeps every voice in the room —
the mode for a microphone several people share. ``voice_focus`` also
removes competing *voices*, keeping only the one it judges primary, which
is what a single-speaker setup wants and what a shared microphone must
avoid: to it, the second person is background.

The filter sits ahead of the model on the inbound path, so it also shapes
what the model's own turn-taking hears. ``off`` is the default — an
integrator who never asked for filtering should not pay its endpointing
cost.
NoiseCancellation.title: NoiseCancellation

OpenAILiveDelegation.description:
Where GPT Live sends the work it decides a turn needs. The voice
model itself only listens and speaks.
OpenAILiveDelegation.title: OpenAILiveDelegation

OpenAILiveModel.description:
OpenAI's GPT Live full-duplex voice model. It listens and speaks at
once and decides itself when each turn starts and ends, so no turn
detector is tunable here; tool calls and reasoning are delegated to a
backend Responses model, which is what the knobs configure. Audio only:
a session on it ignores video and screen frames. A ``voice_…`` id on the agent's ``voice`` selects an authorized
custom voice.

delegation.description:
Who does the work the voice model hands off. ``None`` is
``responses``. Under ``client`` and ``cosmo`` the ``responses_*`` knobs
are unused and the agent may declare no tools.

max_output_tokens.description:
Cap on tokens one delegated response may generate. ``None`` keeps
OpenAI's default.

model_id.description: Concrete GPT Live model to run. ``None`` runs the provider default.

parallel_tool_calls.description:
Whether one delegated turn may call several tools at once. ``None``
keeps OpenAI's default.

provider.description:
Names the provider this block configures. Always ``openai_live``;
the SDKs stamp it, so you never write it yourself.

reasoning_effort.description:
How hard the Responses model reasons on delegated work. ``None``
keeps OpenAI's default.

responses_instructions.description:
Instructions for the Responses model, distinct from the voice model's.
``None`` gives it the agent's own instructions.

responses_model.description:
The Responses model tool calls and reasoning are delegated to, from
the server's allowlist of small tiers; a model outside it is rejected at
session start. ``None`` runs the provider default.

service_tier.description:
OpenAI processing tier for delegated work. ``None`` keeps
OpenAI's default.

tool_choice.description:
Whether a delegated turn must call a tool. ``None`` lets the model
decide (``auto``).

verbosity.description:
How much the Responses model writes back for the voice model to say.
``None`` keeps OpenAI's default.

OpenAILiveModel.title: OpenAILiveModel

OpenAILiveReasoningEffort.description:
How hard the Responses model behind GPT Live reasons on delegated
work (tool calls and lookups). Lower effort answers sooner; ``None``
keeps OpenAI's default.
OpenAILiveReasoningEffort.title: OpenAILiveReasoningEffort

OpenAILiveServiceTier.description: OpenAI processing tier for the Responses model behind GPT Live.
OpenAILiveServiceTier.title: OpenAILiveServiceTier

OpenAILiveToolChoice.description:
Whether the Responses model behind GPT Live must call a tool on each
delegated turn.
OpenAILiveToolChoice.title: OpenAILiveToolChoice

OpenAILiveVerbosity.description:
How much the Responses model behind GPT Live writes back for the
voice model to say. ``LOW`` keeps delegated answers short.
OpenAILiveVerbosity.title: OpenAILiveVerbosity

OpenAIMiniModel.description:
The OpenAI-Realtime mini tier — the same API as
``OpenAIModel`` on a faster, cheaper model, and equally
untunable today.

model_id.description: Concrete mini-tier model to run. ``None`` runs the provider default.

provider.description:
Names the provider this block configures. Always ``openai_mini``;
the SDKs stamp it, so you never write it yourself.

OpenAIMiniModel.title: OpenAIMiniModel

OpenAIModel.description:
The OpenAI-Realtime provider with its knobs. OpenAI Realtime pins its
own sampling and token limits, so only turn-taking is tunable here.

``turn_detection`` selects which detector runs and decides which of the
remaining knobs apply: ``eagerness`` belongs to ``semantic_vad``, the two
window knobs to ``server_vad``. Sending a knob from the other mode is
rejected at session start rather than silently ignored.

eagerness.description:
How eagerly ``semantic_vad`` closes the user's turn — ``high`` answers
sooner, ``low`` waits longer for them to continue. Valid only with
``turn_detection: semantic_vad``. ``None`` keeps the provider default.

model_id.description:
Concrete OpenAI Realtime model to run. ``None`` runs the provider
default. A model id that is not an OpenAI model is rejected at session
start.

prefix_padding_ms.description:
Audio, in milliseconds, kept from before speech was detected. Valid only
with ``server_vad``. ``None`` keeps the server's default.

provider.description:
Names the provider this block configures. Always ``openai``;
the SDKs stamp it, so you never write it yourself.

silence_duration_ms.description:
Silence, in milliseconds, that ends the user's turn. Valid only with
``server_vad``. ``None`` keeps the server's default.

turn_detection.description:
Which turn detector runs. ``semantic_vad`` ends the turn as soon as the
utterance reads as complete rather than after a fixed silence window.
``None`` keeps the provider default (``server_vad``).

OpenAIModel.title: OpenAIModel

PointAtObjectToolSpec.description:
Opt-in to the server-executed object locator, which returns points.

The sibling of ``detect_objects``: a marked point says one thing where
a box around a leaf includes everything behind it. Same zero-config and
availability terms.
PointAtObjectToolSpec.title: PointAtObjectToolSpec

ProviderCapabilities.description:
Which realtime model providers the caller may select per session.

Clients that surface a provider picker should hide it when
``openai_provider_available`` is false — a picker the server would
silently override is worse than no picker.

openai_provider_available.description:
Whether this workspace may select the OpenAI providers (``openai``,
``openai_mini``, ``openai_live``): the server has an OpenAI key and the
plan includes them.

ProviderCapabilities.title: ProviderCapabilities

ReadyEvent.description: Sent after the upstream session is established and the agent is ready.

agent.description:
Resolved registry-agent summary (see ``ResolvedAgent``).
``None`` for inline / default-agent sessions.

max_session_seconds.description:
Effective server-enforced session duration cap, so clients can render
their own countdown. ``None`` = no cap. The server also pushes
``session-ending-soon`` near the deadline and ``session-ended`` at
cutoff.

rejected_tools.description:
Tools this session could not get — a registered tool the deployment
or workspace cannot run right now — with the reason for each. The session
starts without them, so check this to see what it is actually running.

Only availability drops appear here. A spec the server considers
malformed — a bad schema, a duplicate or reserved name, a ``kind`` this
flow does not execute — rejects the whole session start with a 422
(``invalid_tool_config``) instead, and never reaches this list.

session_id.description:
Server-assigned id for this session. Clients persist it and pass it back
as ``experimental.resume_session_id`` on a fresh ``session-config`` to
resume after a disconnect.

ReadyEvent.title: ReadyEvent

ReconnectingEvent.description:
Server is transparently rotating the upstream session.

Emitted after the upstream signals an imminent shutdown when the server
has cached a resumption handle and is reopening the model session. The
transport and session state survive the swap; clients can show a brief
"reconnecting…" indicator and otherwise stay put.

seconds_remaining.description:
Rough seconds until the swap completes, when the upstream reports
it. ``None`` when it does not.

ReconnectingEvent.title: ReconnectingEvent

RejectedTool.description:
One tool spec the server refused, with the reason — so a client can
log *why* a spec was dropped instead of debugging silence.

name.description:
What the dropped tool was called — a client tool's declared name, or a
server tool's wire kind.

reason.description:
Why it was unavailable, e.g. a capability this workspace has not
enabled. Free text for logs and display, not a stable code to match
on.

RejectedTool.title: RejectedTool

name.description: The registry agent the session resolved against.

tools.description:
Final effective tool names (registry tools ∪ client-declared tools,
by name).

ResolvedAgent.title: ResolvedAgent

RevokeTokenResponse.description: Result of revoking a minted end-user token.

revoked.description:
Whether the token was revoked. Revoking one already revoked, or one
that has expired, still reports ``true`` — the end state is the same.

RevokeTokenResponse.title: RevokeTokenResponse

Say.description:
Idle-message action for a server hook: `text` = exact words,
`prompt` = model-generated per instruction, both unset = free model speech.

prompt.description:
Instruction the model composes its line from, for wording that follows
what has been said so far. Mutually exclusive with ``text``.

text.description:
Exact words for the assistant to speak. Mutually exclusive with
``prompt``.

Say.title: Say

ScreenLocateToolSpec.description:
Opt-in to the server-executed screen locator.

Resolves a description to an element on the client's shared screen and
hands the model an opaque handle for it, which the model passes to
whichever screen renderer the client declared
(``cosmo_sdk_screen_click_element`` /
``cosmo_sdk_screen_highlight_element``). Not authorable: SDKs emit this
entry mechanically when the host supplies a screen-capture handler, whose
``screen_capture`` RPC the locator drives. Zero-config;
unknown fields are a schema error.

The locator itself has no availability gate.
``cosmo_sdk_screen_click_element`` does — clicking acts on the user's
machine, so it stays behind the desktop-control policy, and a session that
cannot run it starts without it and reports the drop on
``ready.rejected_tools`` under that name.
ScreenLocateToolSpec.title: ScreenLocateToolSpec

SdkInfo.description:
Self-reported identity of the SDK that opened the session.

``name`` is the SDK's registry package name ("cosmo-ai-sdk" on PyPI,
"cosmo-ai" on npm, "cosmo-swift-sdk" for SwiftPM) — with ``version``,
exactly what is installed. Deployed clients keep sending the name they
were built with; a package rename maps the old name onto the new line
server-side.

The pair is a claim, not a fact: it feeds telemetry and, for packages
we ship, support decisions — never authorization or billing. An unknown
or absent identity is bucketed, never refused.

name.description: Registry package name of the SDK, e.g. ``cosmo-ai-sdk``.

SdkInfo.title: SdkInfo

SemanticEagerness.title: SemanticEagerness

ServerEnvelope.description:
Generic chunked carrier for any oversized server message.

Mirror of ``ClientEnvelope`` for the server→client direction.
The server wraps any ``ServerMessage`` whose serialized JSON
exceeds the transport threshold into a sequence of these chunks; the SDK
buffers by ``envelope_id``, base64-decodes + concatenates, and
re-dispatches the inner message through the same handler path as
un-chunked messages.

``data`` is base64 over the UTF-8 bytes of the inner message JSON for
the same reason as the client side: keeps every chunk ASCII-safe so
byte-boundary splits never land mid-codepoint.

data.description: This chunk's slice of the inner message, base64-encoded.

envelope_id.description:
Groups the chunks of one message, so concurrent envelopes do not
interleave.

total.description: How many chunks the message was split into.

ServerEnvelope.title: ServerEnvelope

ServerToolSpec.description:
Opt-in to one server-executed tool by its dot-namespaced name
(e.g. ``"cosmo.web_search"``).

Deprecated and no longer executed anywhere: typed per-tool kinds
(``web_search``, ``examine_image``, ``detect``, ``point``,
``end_call``) supersede the generic name-reference, and the flow that
honored it is gone — a config carrying one is rejected at session start
with a typed 422 (``invalid_tool_config``). ``cosmo.view_state`` /
``cosmo.set_state`` have no typed kinds yet, so they are unreachable
until they gain them.

Server tools execute server-side; the session observes them through the
``tool-call`` / ``tool-dispatch-started`` / ``tool-result`` lifecycle.

kind.description:
The tool kind. Always ``server`` — the deprecated form, which
session start rejects.

name.description:
Dot-namespaced name of the server tool, e.g. ``cosmo.web_search``.
Kept so the wire shape still decodes; use the tool's own typed kind
instead, since a config carrying this one is refused.

ServerToolSpec.title: ServerToolSpec

SessionArtifact.description:
One downloadable recording of a finished session.

``download_url`` is signed and expires; re-request the listing for a
fresh one rather than storing it.

content_type.description: Media type of the file the URL serves.

download_url.description:
Signed URL for the file. It expires — re-request the listing for a
fresh one rather than storing it.

filename.description: Suggested filename for saving the download.

SessionArtifact.title: SessionArtifact

SessionArtifactKind.description: Which composed recording a download URL points at.
SessionArtifactKind.title: SessionArtifactKind

SessionArtifacts.description:
The composed recordings a session left behind.

Only artifacts already materialized in storage are listed, so a
session that recorded no video, or one still running, reports fewer
than a completed audio+video call. ``expires_at`` applies to every
``download_url`` in ``artifacts``.

artifacts.description:
Only the recordings already materialized in storage, so a session that
recorded no video — or one still running — lists fewer than a completed
audio and video call.

expires_at.description: When every ``download_url`` above stops working, epoch seconds.

session_id.description: The session these recordings belong to.

SessionArtifacts.title: SessionArtifacts

SessionConfig.description:
Session-start payload for external sessions — carried on the HTTP
session-start request (or as the first frame on the WS connect path).
The server replies with ``ReadyEvent`` once the agent is up.

Split into the two concerns of a session: ``agent`` (the persona — what the
model is) and ``session`` (per-run transport options). ``sdk`` identifies
the client (see ``SdkInfo``).

agent.description:
The persona to run: defined inline, or a reference to a workspace
catalog agent. Omitted runs the default agent.

sdk.description: Which SDK and version opened the session.

session.description:
Per-run options for this session — storage consents, duration cap,
experimental knobs. Omitted takes every default.

SessionConfig.title: SessionConfig

SessionEndedEvent.description:
The server ended the session on purpose. Published just before the
transport tears down so clients can render a clean terminal state
instead of treating the room drop as a failure. Delivery is
best-effort — the room close may still arrive first.
SessionEndedEvent.title: SessionEndedEvent

SessionEndingSoonEvent.description:
The server will end this session shortly (e.g. the max-duration cap
is about to fire). Clients may show a countdown; the session keeps
running until ``session-ended``.

reason.description:
Stable slug for why the session is ending (e.g.
``"max_session_duration"``). The vocabulary is additive: match the
slugs you know and treat an unfamiliar one as a plain end.

seconds_remaining.description: Seconds until the session is cut, for a countdown.

SessionEndingSoonEvent.title: SessionEndingSoonEvent

SessionImportRequest.description: Bundle for seeding a completed call: transcript + metadata + optional audio.

provider.description: Which model provider ran the imported call, when it is known.

SessionImportRequest.title: SessionImportRequest

SessionParams.description:
Per-run, transport-level options for one session — continuity and other
knobs that vary run-to-run for the same agent. Audio config lives on the
``agent`` block (it's part of the agent, configured once).

experimental.description:
Unstable opt-in knobs (see ``ExperimentalParams``).
May change shape between releases.

max_session_seconds.description:
Requested wall-clock cap on the session, in seconds. The server
resolves the effective cap as the minimum of this and its own limits —
callers can only shorten, never extend. The effective value is echoed
on ``ready``; the server pushes ``session-ending-soon`` near the
deadline and ``session-ended`` at cutoff.

store_audio.description:
Persist this session's audio. Narrowing only: a session may ask for
less storage than the account's consents allow, never more. Unset defers
to ``store_recording``, then to those consents.

store_recording.description:
Persist this session's recording artifacts (audio/video/transcript/tool
events) server-side. ``False`` writes nothing for the run. Unset stores as
much as the account's consents allow. The per-artifact fields below take
precedence over this one where both are sent.

store_transcript.description:
Persist this session's transcript and tool-call events. Same contract
as ``store_audio``.

store_video.description:
Persist this session's screen-share video. Same contract as
``store_audio``. Screenshots have no field of their own and follow
``store_recording``, so turning this off does not stop them.

SessionParams.title: SessionParams

SessionRecord.description:
Developer-facing session record for the external (API-key) data-out
endpoints. Carries only product-agnostic fields — the workspace and the
end user are resolved from the credential, never echoed back.

ended_at.description: When it ended, epoch seconds. Absent while it is still running.

has_resumption_handle.description:
Whether this session stored a resumption handle. Not a promise that a
resume will use it: the server decides that when the resume is requested,
and falls back to seeding the new session with the prior transcript for a
session that ended too long ago. Either way the request is the same —
pass the id as ``experimental.resume_session_id``.

provider.description: Which model provider ran it, once resolved.

started_at.description: When the session started, epoch seconds.

status.description:
Where the session ended up: ``active`` while it runs, ``completed``
when it ended normally, ``error`` when it did not.

SessionRecord.title: SessionRecord

SessionResponse.description:
Connection credentials for a started session.

The client joins the LiveKit room at ``livekit_url`` with ``token``;
``session_id`` correlates the session across API calls and session
events.

livekit_url.description: LiveKit room URL to connect to.

SessionResponse.title: SessionResponse

SessionResponsiveness.description:
Session-level rollups over the turns, so the common question —
was this session slow — is one read rather than an aggregation.

``first_response_latency_ms`` covers session and provider warm-up and
only exists for turn one; it excludes a pre-turn greeting, and
``first_response_agent_greeted`` reports whether there was one.

``first_response_anchor_measured`` says where that latency was timed
from: true anchors it on measured caller audio, false on session state
instead, and null means a blob old enough not to have recorded which.
The two anchors answer different questions, so a series spanning both
is not comparable to itself — read the latency with this, not alone.

first_response_agent_greeted.description:
Whether the agent opened with a greeting. A greeting is excluded from
``first_response_latency_ms``, so this says whether there was one.

first_response_anchor_measured.description:
Where that first latency was timed from: ``true`` anchors it on
measured caller audio, ``false`` on session state instead, and null means
a record old enough not to have written it down. The two anchors answer
different questions, so a series spanning both is not comparable to
itself — read the latency together with this, never alone.

first_response_latency_ms.description:
How long the caller waited for the agent's first reply. Covers session
and provider warm-up, so it is not comparable with the medians above, and
exists only for turn one.

median_eou_delay_ms.description:
Median endpointing delay: how long the detector took to decide each
turn had ended.

median_generation_to_playout_ms.description:
Median gap between the model generating and audio reaching the
transport.

median_response_ms.description: Median time to first token across the session's turns.

p95_response_ms.description: 95th-percentile time to first token — the tail a caller notices.

SessionResponsiveness.title: SessionResponsiveness

SessionStartTimings.description:
Server-side phase breakdown of session start (milliseconds).

Mirrors the ``starter_*`` fields of the "realtime session dispatched"
log line. Echoed to the client so it can emit one joined
startup-waterfall event (server + client phases) keyed by session_id,
instead of leaving the join to log archaeology.

The server produces these on ``/session/start``; the same shape comes
back untrusted on ``connect-timings``, so the bounds hold on both paths.

dispatch_ms.description:
Dispatching the agent to the room. Reports ``0`` when dispatch runs
after the response, where it costs the client nothing.

project_check_ms.description: Resolving and authorizing the calling project.

provider_resolve_ms.description: Choosing the model provider and confirming it is available here.

resolve_ms.description:
Version check, project, provider, tools and limits, resolved
together and reported as one number. The phases folded into it report
``0`` in their own fields rather than a fabricated split, and
``dispatch_ms`` reports ``0`` too — dispatch runs after the response, so
it costs the client nothing.

total_ms.description:
The whole server-side start, end to end. Not the sum of the phases
above — phases folded into ``resolve_ms`` report ``0`` individually.

version_check_ms.description: Checking the client's SDK version against the supported floor.

SessionStartTimings.title: SessionStartTimings

SessionStateWriteEvent.description:
First-party cosmo event: live session state after a ``set_state`` tool
write, for rendering call progress in a client UI. Carries the
full canonical state, not a delta; ``stage`` is hoisted from
``state["stage"]`` and ``warnings`` are the advisory schema findings the
model also saw in its tool result.

stage.description:
``state["stage"]``, lifted out for clients that render call progress.
``None`` when the state carries no stage.

state.description:
The whole state after the write, so the newest event supersedes the
previous one.

updated_keys.description: Just the keys this write touched, for highlighting what changed.

warnings.description:
Advisory schema findings from the write. The model saw these too;
they did not block it.

SessionStateWriteEvent.title: SessionStateWriteEvent

SessionStatus.description: Where a realtime session is in its lifecycle.
SessionStatus.title: SessionStatus

SessionTimeline.description:
When each turn of a session happened and how long its parts took.

The companion to the transcript: that endpoint reports what was said,
this one what happened and when. ``turns`` is ordered oldest first and
is empty unless ``timeline_status`` is ``recorded`` — it carries the
same three states as a session's usage summary, which is written by
the same teardown pass.

responsiveness.description:
Session-level rollups over the turns, so "was this session slow" is one
read rather than an aggregation.

session_id.description: The session this timeline belongs to.

started_at.description:
Session start, the origin every ``at`` is meaningful against — a
timeline is read as offsets, and without this one a caller would have to
fetch the session record to compute them.

timeline_status.description:
Whether the timeline exists yet. Carries the same three states as the
usage summary, which the same teardown pass writes.

turn_count.description:
Model-response turns the session recorded, taken from its stored
summary. Not the length of ``turns``: that list is empty on a session
recorded before per-turn spans were captured, and carries turn-detector
rows the count never included.

turns.description:
The turns, oldest first. Empty unless ``timeline_status`` is
``recorded``.

SessionTimeline.title: SessionTimeline

SessionTokenUsage.description:
Token usage reported by the session's model provider, split by
direction and modality. The live ``cosmo.usage`` event's counters plus
the input and output totals, with the same cumulative semantics.

input_cached_tokens.description:
Input served from the provider's cache. Already counted in
``input_tokens`` — a subset, not an addition.

input_tokens.description: Every input token, across all modalities.

output_audio_tokens.description:
Audio the model produced. On a session running ``audio.output=false``
this depends on the provider: one with a native text-only mode produces
none, while one without keeps generating speech that is discarded, and
those tokens still accrue.

output_tokens.description: Every output token, across all modalities.

total_tokens.description: Input plus output, as the provider reports it.

SessionTokenUsage.title: SessionTokenUsage

SessionTranscriptTurn.description:
One transcript line: timestamp (epoch seconds), speaker role, and text.

Open to unknown keys: this is also the transcript endpoint's response
model, and the server->client direction stays tolerant. The import
request nests a strict variant instead.

ts.description: When the line was spoken, epoch seconds.

SessionTranscriptTurn.title: TranscriptTurn

SessionTurn.description:
One turn's server-measured spans, in milliseconds.

``source`` says which mechanism produced the row and therefore which
spans are set, so a null is "this mechanism does not measure that"
rather than "this turn was instant":

* ``realtime_model`` — one row per model reply. ``ttft_ms`` and
  ``response_duration_ms`` are provider-reported;
  ``generation_to_playout_ms`` and ``playout_duration_ms`` are taken
  from state transitions on one process clock.
* ``pipeline_eou`` — the turn detector's own endpointing figures,
  ``end_of_utterance_delay_ms`` and ``transcription_delay_ms``.

``listening_to_generation_ms`` is the whole window from the agent
returning to listening until the provider's first generation packet.
It contains the caller's own think time and utterance as well as the
turn-detection decision, so it is **not** a measure of how long the
agent took to react — reach for ``ttft_ms`` for that.

Every span is measured on the server, whose clock stops at the frame
handed to the transport. None of them include the listener's playout
hop; only the client is on that side of the network.

at.description:
When the turn happened, epoch seconds — the same clock as the
timeline's ``started_at``. Subtract that to read the timeline as
offsets.

end_of_utterance_delay_ms.description:
The turn detector's own endpointing figure — how long after the
speaker stopped it decided the turn had ended. Set on ``pipeline_eou``
rows.

generation_to_playout_ms.description:
From the first generated packet to the first frame handed to the
transport, taken from state transitions on one process clock.

index.description:
Position of this turn among the model's replies, counting from one.
Null on a row the turn detector produced rather than the model, which is
not numbered.

listening_to_generation_ms.description:
From the agent returning to listening until the provider's first
generation packet. Contains the caller's own think time and utterance as
well as the turn-detection decision, so it is not a measure of agent
reaction time — read ``ttft_ms`` for that.

playout_duration_ms.description: How long the agent's audio played for, on the same clock.

response_duration_ms.description:
How long the provider spent generating the reply. Set on
``realtime_model`` rows.

source.description:
Which mechanism produced this row, and therefore which spans below are
set. A null span means this mechanism does not measure that, not that the
turn was instant.

transcription_delay_ms.description:
How long the transcription lagged the audio. Set on ``pipeline_eou``
rows.

ttft_ms.description:
Time to the provider's first generated token. The closest measure of
how long the agent took to react. Set on ``realtime_model`` rows.

SessionTurn.title: SessionTurn

SessionUsage.description:
Usage summary for one session, in provider-reported units.

``duration_seconds`` is set once the session ends. The rest of the
detail arrives with the summary, so it is present only while
``usage_status`` is ``RECORDED``, at which point the numbers are
final. ``tokens`` is absent when the provider reports none.

agent_speaking_seconds.description: How long the agent was speaking.

duration_seconds.description: Wall-clock length of the session, set once it ends.

model.description: The concrete model id that ran, which a family alias resolves to.

provider.description:
Which model provider actually ran the session, after the server
resolved the requested model.

status.description: Where the session itself ended up.

tokens.description:
The token breakdown. Absent when the provider reported none — that is
absence of reporting, not zero usage.

turn_count.description: How many turns the session took.

usage_status.description:
Whether the usage summary exists yet. Poll while this is ``pending``;
stop on ``unavailable``.

user_speaking_seconds.description: How long the user was speaking.

SessionUsage.title: SessionUsage

SilenceTimeout.description:
Server-runtime hook: perform `action` after `timeout_seconds` of user
silence.

action.description: What to do when the timeout fires — speak a line, or end the call.

max_count.description:
How many times this hook may fire, 1–10, so a silent caller is not
prompted forever. Counted per run of silence when ``reset_mode`` is
``on_user_speech``, and across the session when it is ``never``.

name.description:
Label for this hook, for your own reference and the server's logs. It
is not carried on the event the hook fires, so a session running several
silence hooks cannot tell from the event which one fired.

How much to widen ``timeout_seconds`` once the caller has spoken at
least once, 1–10, so a present but quiet caller waits longer than a line
that was silent from the start. ``1`` waits the same either way. Omit to
use the server's default.

Whether the fire count resets. ``never`` counts across the whole
session; ``on_user_speech`` starts over each time the user speaks.

Seconds of user silence before the action runs, 1–1000. Scaled by
``present_multiplier`` once the caller has spoken at least once.

Opt-in to the server-kept speaker log of the room.

The server runs a diarizing transcript of the room's audio beside the
model and offers a tool that reads the last few seconds of it back,
one stable label per voice (``S0``, ``S1``, …); the model binds labels
to people from what they say about themselves. Zero-config; unknown
fields are a schema error. Availability is checked at session start: a
deployment that cannot run the transcript starts the session without
it and reports the drop on ``ready.rejected_tools``.

Reasoning depth the client may request for the Gemini realtime model.

Mirrors ``google.genai.types.ThinkingLevel`` (minus the unspecified
sentinel). The server maps it onto the upstream enum; ``None`` on the init
leaves the server default in place.

ToolCallEvent.description:
Model decided to invoke a server-executed tool.

Three-event lifecycle:
  ``tool-call`` (model decided)
    → ``tool-dispatch-started`` (server-side handler began)
    → ``tool-result`` (completed).

name.description: Name of the tool being invoked.

tool_call_id.description:
Stable per-invocation id (the upstream's function-call id). Use this
to correlate the ``tool-call`` / ``tool-dispatch-started`` /
``tool-result`` triple for one invocation. Distinct from the
message-level ``id``.

ToolCallEvent.title: ToolCallEvent

ToolDispatchStartedEvent.description:
Server-side handler for the tool call began executing.

Sits between ``tool-call`` and ``tool-result`` to let UIs show a
"dispatching…" state — useful for slow tools where the gap between
model decision and result is multiple seconds.

name.description: Name of the tool that started executing.

tool_call_id.description: Correlates with the ``tool-call`` that opened this invocation.

ToolDispatchStartedEvent.title: ToolDispatchStartedEvent

ToolInvocationEvent.description:
Server asks the connected client to run a tool locally.

Sent only for tools declared via ``kind="client"`` specs at session
start. The SDK runs the tool against the client's local resources and
returns the result out of band; the server validates it before
resolving the pending dispatch.

``request_id`` is the dispatch correlation id; ``tool_call_id`` is the
upstream's identifier for the underlying function call and is kept
distinct so observability messages (``tool-call`` / ``tool-result``)
still correlate by the upstream's id.

``origin`` identifies which producer authored the invocation:
``"realtime"`` for the voice model (default), ``"server"`` for a
server tool runtime reaching back through the same bridge. Clients
that don't render the distinction can ignore the field.

``executable`` is ``False`` for an informational mirror whose execution
runs out-of-band; ``True`` (default, and for a missing field) means the
recipient runs the tool.

args.description: Arguments the model produced, matching the tool's declared schema.

executable.description:
Whether the recipient should run the tool. ``False`` marks an
informational mirror of a call executed elsewhere.

name.description: Name of the client tool to run.

origin.description:
Who asked: ``realtime`` for the live model, ``server`` for a
server-side runtime reaching the same tool.

request_id.description:
Identifies this notification. Minted fresh for the event and
unrelated to the call's own transport-level request, so it is not a
handle to reply on — client tools are invoked and answered over the
transport's RPC channel, and this event only mirrors that.

tool_call_id.description:
The model's own id for the call, shared with the ``tool-call``
lifecycle.

ToolInvocationEvent.title: ToolInvocationEvent

ToolJobResult.description:
A long-running client tool finished off-band and is delivering its
terminal result. The server resolves the original tool call from
``job_id`` and injects the outcome; ``summary`` / ``error`` are the
model-facing text and ``result`` is structured data for logging.

Half of the background client-tool primitive — a tool whose work outlives
the RPC reply budget acks first and lands its outcome here. Every SDK
implements it, so it is protocol vocabulary rather than a first-party
extension.

error.description:
Model-facing text for a failed job — what the assistant is told went
wrong.

job_id.description:
Identifies the job this result belongs to — the id the acked tool call
was given.

result.description:
Structured outcome. Accepted for forward compatibility but not
consumed today — only ``status`` and ``summary``/``error`` reach the
model, so put anything the agent must act on in those.

status.description: Whether the work succeeded. ``failed`` pairs with ``error``.

summary.description:
Model-facing text for a completed job — what the assistant is told
came back.

tool_name.description: Name of the tool that ran, for logging and attribution.

ToolJobResult.title: ToolJobResult

ToolResultEvent.description: Server-side tool finished. ``summary`` is a short human-readable line.

summary.description: Short human-readable line about the outcome, for display.

tool_call_id.description: Correlates with the ``tool-call`` that opened this invocation.

TranscriptDeltaEvent.description:
Streaming transcript event for either speaker.

For the assistant role in audio sessions, this is the audio
transcription — the words the listener actually heard. The model may
ALSO emit a separate text channel via ``ModelTextEvent``; consumers
that render a "what was spoken" bubble should subscribe to
``transcript`` only.

Contract (wire-level, applies to both user and assistant):

* Streaming events (``is_final=False``): ``text`` is the **new
  fragment since the previous event** for that role's turn (a
  delta). Consumers append.
* Terminating event (``is_final=True``): ``text`` is the
  **cumulative full transcript** for the turn. Consumers replace
  whatever they accumulated with this value.

Two carve-outs where the terminating event is NOT the full turn, both
load-bearing rather than accidental:

* **Empty final.** A turn the model produced nothing usable for (a
  suppressed or garbled turn) finalizes with ``text=""``. It means an
  empty turn, not "unchanged" — a consumer that skips empty finals
  leaves the turn's bubble dangling into the next one.
* **Suffix final on a silent session.** When the agent runs with
  ``audio.output=False``, a user final that arrives after the VAD
  endpoint already committed the utterance is stripped of the committed
  prefix, so it carries only the remainder. Replacing on final would
  drop the part committed at the endpoint.

A consumer that only ever appends non-finals and replaces on final is
correct for the common path; these two need the extra handling.

is_final.description:
Whether this closes the turn. Append while it is false; on true,
replace what you accumulated — except in the two cases the class
docstring describes, where the final carries less than the whole turn
and replacing loses text.

role.description: Who was speaking — the user, or the assistant.

text.description:
The new fragment while ``is_final`` is false, the whole turn once it
is true. The class docstring names the two cases where a final carries
less than the whole turn.

TranscriptDeltaEvent.title: TranscriptDeltaEvent

voice.

stability.description:
ElevenLabs only, ``0``–``1``: lower varies delivery more between

ElevenLabs only: boost similarity to the reference speaker, at some

TurnCompleteEvent.title: TurnCompleteEvent

TurnDetectionMode.description:
Which turn detector ends the user's turn.

``server_vad`` ends the turn on a fixed silence window;
``semantic_vad`` runs OpenAI's classifier that ends it as soon as the
utterance reads as complete (OpenAI-only); ``cosmo_vad`` runs Cosmo's own
semantic detector in the realtime worker (Gemini-only). ``None`` keeps
the provider default: ``server_vad`` on OpenAI and Grok, ``cosmo_vad``
on Gemini.

UsageEvent.description:
First-party cosmo event: cumulative token usage for the live session,
split by direction and modality. Emitted for any external session whose
upstream reports usage — translation is stateless, not gated on the
``cosmo`` config block.

input_audio_tokens.description: Audio tokens sent to the model so far this session.

input_cached_tokens.description:
Input tokens served from the provider's cache, already counted in the
input totals above.

input_image_tokens.description: Image tokens sent to the model so far this session.

input_text_tokens.description: Text tokens sent to the model so far this session.

output_audio_tokens.description: Audio tokens the model produced so far this session.

output_text_tokens.description: Text tokens the model produced so far this session.

total_tokens.description: Every token counted above, as the provider reports the total.

UsageEvent.title: UsageEvent

UsageStatus.description:
Whether a session's detailed usage summary is available.

``PENDING`` while the session runs and for a short window after it
ends, before the summary is written. ``RECORDED`` once it is there
and the numbers are final. ``UNAVAILABLE`` once that window has
passed without one arriving: a session with no turn or speech
activity records none, and neither does one torn down abnormally.
UsageStatus.title: UsageStatus

UserSpeechTimeoutEvent.description:
A server-runtime silence timeout fired: the user was silent past a
configured threshold and the server performed `action`. Observability only.

action.description: What the server did in response.

max_count.description:
The hook's nudge ceiling. It goes quiet after the last one rather
than escalating; under ``reset_mode: on_user_speech`` the count resets on
user speech, so this bounds one run of silence, not the session.

silence_ms.description:
Silence accrued in the window that fired. The clock restarts after
each firing, so on a second or later nudge this measures from the
previous one, not from the last time the user spoke.

trigger_count.description:
Which firing this is in the current run, from one. Under
``reset_mode: on_user_speech`` the count restarts when the user speaks,
so it can return to one within a session.

UserStartedSpeakingEvent.description:
Server-side VAD detected user voice activity start.

Information-only — clients use this for UI indicators (mic-level
highlight, "listening…" label). Does NOT change client mic behavior;
the mic keeps streaming continuously so overlapping speech is captured.
UserStartedSpeakingEvent.title: UserStartedSpeakingEvent

UserStoppedSpeakingEvent.description:
Server-side VAD detected the end of user voice activity.

Information-only, the counterpart to ``user-started-speaking``: it ends
the "listening…" indicator. It does not mean the turn is over — the
turn detector decides that separately.
UserStoppedSpeakingEvent.title: UserStoppedSpeakingEvent

VerifyResponse.description:
Result of a credential preflight — a 200 means the credential
authenticated; the fields say what it can do from here.

can_start_sessions.description: Whether this credential carries the scope a session start needs. False means the credential is valid but under-scoped.

realtime_voice_available.description: Whether this deployment has the default voice stack configured — LiveKit plus the default provider's key. style. One sub-object shared by both agent variants.

per session — the voice then drifts between connects. Clients that want

Caller-supplied "how to speak" instruction text, appended to the system

WebSearchToolSpec.description:
Opt-in to the server-executed web-search tool, as its own typed kind.

The server owns the model-facing declaration (name, description, query
schema) — the client only opts in, so the spec carries no fields today.

name-reference, which is deprecated and rejected at session start.

deployment or workspace that cannot run the tool starts the session
without it and reports the drop on ``ready.rejected_tools``.
